points.description: mRNA leaves the nucleus through a nuclear pore and travels through the cytoplasm to a ribosome (or enters the rough ER).
Initiation/codon reading: the ribosome reads the mRNA bases in triplets (codons), starting at a START codon in the P site.

tRNA with the complementary anticodon recognizes and pairs with each mRNA codon, and its amino acid is bonded to the adjacent tRNA's amino acid; a new tRNA/amino acid is then added (elongation), building the chain.
Termination: amino acids continue to be linked until a STOP codon is read in the A site, ending the protein.

rubric.notes: Full marks for four steps in order, each correctly described: exit/travel to ribosome, codon reading/initiation, tRNA pairing and peptide bonding (elongation), stop codon termination. Equivalent wording accepted. Partial marks for steps named but not described.
